chapters.title: Review personally under every CLEAR category
chapters.transcript:
Bring back the communication you saved in Lesson Two Point Two. Keep the original version beside you. Before asking AI to critique it, read it yourself. What does the recipient need? Which statements could affect a decision? Which details require a source? Your own review comes first because you know the purpose and carry responsibility for the result.

The Academy uses CLEAR quality review. Each letter names a different question. Correct checks facts, names, dates, numbers, and instructions. Listener checks whether the communication serves its audience. Enough checks for missing information and unnecessary repetition. Appropriate checks whether the tone fits the setting. Responsible checks privacy, fairness, risk, authority, and accountability. Use all five. A message can pass one category and fail another.

Start with Correct. Underline claims that can be checked. Delivery in five days is a claim. An appointment is confirmed is a claim. Compare exact wording with an approved record. Check conditions as well as numbers. A policy that allows review within two business days after complete information arrives does not promise a completed estimate in two days.

For Listener, read as the intended recipient. A customer needs a clear next action. A manager may need status, a decision, and the owner of the follow-up. Ask whether unfamiliar language makes the reader guess. For Enough, check whether the message includes what that person needs to act. Remove repetition only when it adds no useful meaning. Shorter is helpful when the necessary detail survives.

For Appropriate, examine courtesy, tone, and the situation. A missing detail can be requested without blaming the customer. A serious limit should not be hidden behind cheerful language. For Responsible, examine who may see the information and who may make the promise. A private note about a customer does not belong in a shared email. A drafting assistant cannot approve an appointment or capacity commitment.

Record one finding under each category, even when your finding is that no change is needed. Explain why. Do not simply mark five boxes and call the work reviewed. A useful review names the sentence, the concern, and the next action. This creates a record of your judgment before AI adds its suggestions.

chapters.title: Compare AI critique with your own judgment
chapters.transcript:
After your personal review, ask your own AI assistant for additional critique. Give it the draft, the purpose, the intended audience, and only the source material you are authorized to share. Remove private details that are not needed. If a source is confidential, use an approved extract or describe the relevant rule without exposing the full record.

The approved request asks the assistant to critique under Correct, Listener, Enough, Appropriate, and Responsible. It must flag unsupported claims and missing information. It must not assert that facts are verified. This distinction matters. Critique can suggest what to examine. Verification requires you to compare the claim with evidence that can actually support it.

Imagine our fictional service business draft says: Your estimate is approved, and we guarantee delivery in five days. Please provide the outstanding specifications immediately so we can action the deliverable. The first sentence creates an approval and a delivery promise. The second uses unfamiliar language, sounds demanding, and does not say which specifications are missing. The draft can sound professional while failing several CLEAR questions.

An AI critique might catch the five-day promise but miss the invented approval. It might recommend replacing guarantee with expect. That changes the tone without establishing capacity. It might remove the request for details to make the message shorter. That would remove the action the customer needs to take. Treat each suggestion as something to examine, not something to accept automatically.

Compare the model's suggestions with your own review. Where do they agree? What did the assistant notice that you missed? What did you notice that it missed? Which suggestion would make the result less accurate or useful? Record at least one decision about a suggestion and explain your reason. You may accept, revise, or reject it.

Asking the same model whether its answer is correct is not independent evidence. Asking another model can provide another opinion, but agreement between models still does not prove the claim. A confident statement that a policy is verified is only output unless you examine the actual approved policy and confirm that it supports the exact wording.

Keep the critique and your decisions together. The aim is a better review, with you still directing the work. If the assistant supplies a source link, open and examine the source before relying on it. If the source is unavailable or does not support the claim, keep the claim unresolved and decide whether to verify it elsewhere, qualify it accurately, or remove it.

chapters.title: Verify a material claim against an approved source
chapters.transcript:
Choose at least one material claim from your draft. Material means it could change what someone believes, decides, or does. A date, price, deadline, approval, safety instruction, or delivery promise may be material. Write the exact sentence you intend to check so the review does not drift into a different question.

Choose a source that has authority over that claim. An approved business record can establish an internal commitment. The responsible organization's current notice can establish its own event details. A project owner may confirm an authorized deadline. A general article about typical delivery times cannot establish that your team has capacity to deliver this particular job in five days.

Our continuing fictional example uses a practice record, not a real company policy. The fictional intake record says that room dimensions and a preferred appointment date are missing. Complete requests are reviewed within two business days. Appointment booking requires the scheduling owner's approval. A completed estimate and five-day delivery are not confirmed. Label this record as fictional in your practice evidence.

Compare the draft with that record. Your estimate is approved is unsupported. Delivery in five days is unsupported. Even we expect delivery in five days would still suggest a capacity expectation that the record does not establish. Remove the promise or replace it with an accurate statement that the schedule will be confirmed after review. Do not soften an invented fact until it seems acceptable.

Check the scope and date of the source. Does it apply to this request? Is it the approved version? Does an exception change the conclusion? Record the source title or record identifier, its date or version when available, the date you checked it, and the specific detail supporting your decision. If the source date is unknown, say so rather than inventing one.

Your result may be supported, contradicted, or unresolved. Supported means the evidence matches the claim within its stated limits. Contradicted means the source says something different. Unresolved means the available evidence is insufficient. Verification can establish a limit; it does not have to produce approval.

Apply this to your own project communication. Protect private sources. Save only the approved citation or necessary extract, not an entire confidential file. If an important claim cannot be checked, explain the limit and keep the communication from being used as though the claim were settled. A clear source record makes your revision explainable to another person.

chapters.title: Revise, obtain human approval, and retain the evidence
chapters.transcript:
Now revise the communication using your CLEAR findings, your decisions about AI critique, and the source check. Fix factual meaning before polishing style. A better sentence must say something you can support. It must also serve the recipient and stay within the sender's authority.

For the fictional estimate message, a responsible revision might read: Thank you for your estimate request. Please reply with the room dimensions and your preferred appointment date. After we receive complete information, our team will review your request within two business days. We will confirm the estimate and schedule after the appropriate review. No appointment or delivery date is confirmed by this message.

This version names the missing details, preserves the condition that complete information must arrive, and removes unsupported approval and delivery promises. The courtesy helps the customer respond. The limits help prevent a misunderstanding. Check every CLEAR category again after revising because one correction can introduce a different problem.

Human approval is a separate decision. Name the person or role with authority to approve the message and any commitments it contains. A person authorized to review wording may not have authority to confirm capacity, prices, or appointments. AI critique does not grant either kind of authority. Your practice record should state whether approval was obtained or remains pending.

When approval has not been obtained, retain the work as a reviewed draft awaiting approval. Do not label it approved simply because the activity is complete. For fictional practice, describe the simulated approval route and clearly state that no real approval or sending occurred. This lesson does not require contacting anyone or sending the communication.

Your applied check includes a draft with an invented fact, an unsuitable audience tone, and a missing next action. Correct all three and explain who could approve the result. Changing only the factual sentence leaves the reader problem unresolved. Changing only the tone leaves the false commitment in place. Show how each change helps.

Save the original draft, your five CLEAR findings, the AI critique, your decisions about its suggestions, the exact material claim, source and check date, revised communication, approval status, and remaining limits in Prompt and Communication Evidence within your continuing Project Record. Use the workbook for your study notes and reflection. Preserve the communication from Lesson Two Point Two as the before version.

In Lesson Two Point Four, you will compare assistants, automation, agents, and a no-AI alternative for your workflow. The reviewed communication gives you a concrete example of AI support and human control. Today, your progress is work you can trace to evidence, revise for its audience, and hold for the right human approval.

demos.title: Apply all five CLEAR questions
demos.transcript: We review this fictional draft ourselves before asking AI. The estimate approval and five-day delivery promise lack support. The tone pressures the customer, and outstanding specifications does not name the missing details. CLEAR also asks whether the message contains private information and whether the sender has authority to make its commitments.

demos.title: Compare critique without treating it as proof
demos.transcript: The assistant suggests replacing guaranteed with expected. We reject that change because the fictional record confirms no five-day capacity. We retain its useful suggestion to name the missing details. AI critique adds questions and possible revisions. It does not verify the facts or authorize the promise.

Examine an approved record before using a material claim.

demos.title: Check the claim against its source
demos.transcript: We compare the exact delivery claim with the fictional approved intake record. The record confirms review within two business days after complete inputs arrive. It does not confirm estimate approval, appointment booking, or five-day delivery. We remove the unsupported commitment and record the source, the check date, and the remaining limit.

demos.title: Revise and preserve the approval boundary
demos.transcript: The revised fictional message asks for room dimensions and a preferred appointment date. It preserves the complete-input condition and removes invented approval and delivery promises. We identify the scheduling owner for appointment approval. The Project Record keeps the original, CLEAR findings, source check, revised draft, approval status, and remaining limits. Completing practice does not send or approve a real message.
